candidate.answerReason: The hour hand is one quarter of the way from 2 to 3, leaving three quarters of a 30-degree interval to the minute hand.

methods.label: Track the hour hand between marks
methods.explanation:
The hour hand moves steadily between hour marks, so at \(2{:}15\) it has already moved beyond \(2\). Adjacent hour marks are separated by \(360^\circ/12=30^\circ\).

The minute hand points to \(3\). Since \(15\) minutes is \(15/60=\frac14\) of an hour, the hour hand is one quarter of the way from \(2\) to \(3\). The smaller angle between the hands is the remaining three quarters of that interval:
\[
\frac34\cdot30^\circ=22\frac12^\circ.
\]
The answer is choice C.
methods.levelReason: Equal clock divisions, a fraction of an hour, and elementary angle arithmetic suffice.

candidate.annotationRationale: The target is calculating the angle between two moving rays. Uniform hour-hand motion uses direct proportion, supported by the conversion between hours and minutes. Angular minute and second conversions are not used.
